changeRequest: add a lamp post near the workshop

result.reasoning: The request assumes: (1) a lampPost object type exists — confirmed; (2) a workshop building exists — confirmed as a building type; (3) outdoor placement near buildings is possible — confirmed via placements with location='outdoors' and plot coordinates. This matches the cheap operation of placing another instance of an existing object type.

result.understoodIntent: Add one more lamp post (an existing outdoor prop type) placed near the workshop building, purely as a new entry in the placements list — no new object type, no new behavior.
result.willBuild: Append a single new entry to the placements array: a lampPost-type object with location "outdoors" and a plot position chosen to sit just outside the workshop building (whose plot is {x:2, y:2}) — e.g. plot {x:1.7, y:1.7}, close enough to read as "near the workshop" without overlapping its footprint or the existing lamp-2 placement at {x:1.4, y:0.6}. Uses the existing lampPost recipe and default colour/light settings from OBJECT_TYPES unchanged. No changes to objectTypes, buildings, chooseAction, applyAction, or tick.

criteria.description: The lampPost object type still exists in the registry returned by initialWorld (unaffected by the placement addition).
initialWorld().placements grows by at least one entry compared to its current 18-item baseline, reflecting the new lamp post placement.
A lampPost placement (the type used for the new instance) draws without throwing.

Running tick() ten times in sequence from a minimal hand-built world (tick/money/sims only, no placements dependency) produces the same sequence of results as the pre-change baseline, since tick/chooseAction/applyAction never read placements.
applyAction with action 'eat' on a minimal hand-built world (no placements) still restores hunger and charges money identically to the pre-change baseline.

result.willNotTouch: chooseAction, applyAction, tick, the objectTypes registry (lampPost's recipe/light/colour stay default), buildings, sims, surfaces, and every existing placement including the current two lamp posts (lamp-1, lamp-2).

stages.reviewText:
Kitchen Sink: **Yes** — it made broad, unrelated formatting rewrites (OBJECT_TYPES/placements/surfaces JSON-style quoting) instead of only appending one placement entry.

Wrong Abstraction: **No** — no new logic was introduced or duplicated; core functions remain single-source and unchanged.

Optimistic Path: **No** — no new execution-path logic was added, so no new edge-case handling gaps were introduced.

Runaway Refactor: **No** — despite noisy reformatting, there is no added architectural or algorithmic complexity.

[NIT] Large non-functional reformatting of unrelated data blocks creates avoidable diff noise and review risk for a change that only needed a single placements append.
